### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a64f512ea521aa4fe37de6438303c23cd0b31d60` — the merge of head `616735ceb85dcd23b446d4fa6d5175b90aa0a4ed` into base `529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a64f512ea521aa4fe37de6438303c23cd0b31d60 && git checkout a64f512ea521aa4fe37de6438303c23cd0b31d60
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234 616735ceb85dcd23b446d4fa6d5175b90aa0a4ed && git checkout -B drift-repro 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234 && git merge --no-ff 616735ceb85dcd23b446d4fa6d5175b90aa0a4ed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `89dff98f61dd45bc47bef8b17d358db26676a759`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-summary-rollback.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts

Inputs read: card #33699 body and all 10 comments (rulings 6893104201 and 6893661036, reports 6892420600, 6893257535, 6895711951), the PR body, the net diff `45dee177..89dff98f` (9 files), the 66 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read on `origin/main`, never reviewed: plugin-security `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts`, `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`; plugin-sharing `sharing-plugin.ts`, `record-share-cascade.ts`; plugin-auth `last-admin-guard.ts`; objectql `engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, `recycle-bin/capture.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `packages/spec`: unchanged. Named right.** `hook.zod.ts` moves two TSDoc blocks only (`dispatch.mode`, `referentialCascadeDelete`); no `z.` shape, no `.describe()` string, no generated artifact. `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Type Check · consumer gates` are green.
- **Published runtime contract of `HookContext` for a cascaded child delete: narrowed. Named right, with one omission (N3).** `dispatch.mode` 'record' → 'per-row', `dispatch.index` 0..N-1 within the chunk, one shared `dispatch.scope` per chunk, `input.options` from `{ where: { id } }` to `{ where: { id: { $in } }, multi: true }`, and the chunk's `beforeDelete`s all run before its one set delete. The changeset and the `dispatch.mode` TSDoc say so. Not named: `ctx.result` in `afterDelete` moves from the driver's by-id answer to absent (`buildPerRowAfterContexts` passes no payload on a delete).
- **Public package surface of `@objectstack/objectql`: unchanged. Named right.** `CascadeBatchNarrowed`, `cascadeBatchIdsOf` and the `ids` member of `CascadeIssuedDelete` are exported from `engine-top-level.ts` to its sibling section modules only; `src/index.ts` does not re-export that module.
- **Realtime, recycle bin, hook ceiling: unchanged. Named right.** A claimed batch publishes one `data.record.deleted` per pre-image row; `openRecycleBinCapture` is reached only on the by-id branch and a child that joins `cascadeDeleteSets` opens none, so the bin stays one entry per root; a chunk is `REFERENCE_PROBE_BATCH` (500), under `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` and under every plugin bound I read (last-admin `DEFAULT_MAX_SCAN` 1000, comment `MULTI_WRITE_AUTH_LIMIT` 1000, `PREDICATE_WRITE_READABLE_ID_CAP` 10,000).
- **"A permission refusal rolls the whole cascade back" (changeset, Unchanged): named WRONG for one direction.** See M1.
- **Gate verdicts.** 65 of 66 check-runs are success or skipped. `Test Core (3/8)` (run 132839243301) was `in_progress` when this record was written: it is not a verdict yet, and report 6895711951's triage of its earlier failure (an `@objectstack/mcp` CPU-budget case) is the dev's account, not a check-run conclusion. The adopting seat reads its conclusion before anything is queued.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/33699-cascade-delete-batch.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. Right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, accepted value, requirement, default or meaning of an authored key moves; what moves is an engine-produced context a handler reads. AGENTS.md step 3: `none` takes patch, and a breaking non-protocol change ships patch with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. Both are present: the `**BREAKING**` paragraph with a FROM → TO mapping and the remedy, and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker whose reason is true of the diff. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm: a hook that read `dispatch.mode === 'record'`, a by-id `input.options`, or its siblings' absence on a cascaded child loses that. The line is byte-identical in the changeset, the PR body and claim 6893695718. The `!` in the title matches.
- Ruling 6893661036 "Declare it" is met in the changeset: the `dispatch.mode` change, the sibling-count flip with `options.multi` / `referentialCascadeDelete` as the remedy, and the fallback keeping today's shape so one cascade can show both.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in report 6895711951. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, plugin-auth test outside the objectql claim surface: accepted. It is the proof ruling 6893661036 leans on (the shipped guard judges the whole batch), it is test-only, and objectql cannot import plugin-auth.
- Deviation, lint over touched files only and downstream suites left to CI: answered by the head's check-runs (`Lint · ESLint`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` 1, 2, 4 to 8 of 8 green), except shard 3/8, open as in ①.
- Deviation, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally: answered, `Build Core` is green.
- Deviation, the bench "before" run stamped with the branch commit: accepted. 155 statements matches the independent reading on the card at `d7e1a5aa` (6892420600); 57 is the dev's own run. Ruling precondition (2), a measured count replacing the estimate, is met.
- Deviation, changeset `Clause-②` line corrected before `pr_create`: verified verbatim at this head.
- **Ruling precondition (1) is NOT met: escalate to the seat.** #33782 is open, labelled `pm:dispatched`, with no PR. The PR body says landing waits on it and the PR is a draft; that holds the queue, it does not answer M1.
- **Out-of-scope finding "never more rows ... #33782's pin, noted, not filed": not accepted as carried.** It is a property of this diff's own claim, and I found a concrete path. See M1.
- **Out-of-scope finding c1 "noted, not filed": escalate to the seat.** Ruling 6893104201 bound this card to "plus c1 (the engine merges its three identical reads)", ruling 6893661036 kept everything but point 4, and `Fixes #33699` closes the card with c1 undone and no carrier. It needs a follow-up card, or the closing keyword changed, before merge. No effect on the contract.
- Security label: no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`; nothing to add on that rule.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself holds against ruling 6893661036 (F1).** `deleteCascadedChildren` issues `delete(child, { where: { id: { $in: chunk } }, multi: true, context })` per 500 dependents; the predicate arm gives each row `dispatch.mode: 'per-row'`, runs every `beforeDelete`, one set delete, then every `afterDelete`. The token claim is exact: `claimReferentialCascadeDelete` matches only a `where` that is precisely `{ id: { $in } }` over the same id set, is taken before any middleware or hook, and is single-use, so a hook's own delete inside the dispatch is never marked; a by-id token refuses an object-shaped target as before. Grandchildren join the root's set through `cascadeDeleteSets` and get a token of their own. The `entered` bookkeeping covers a row reached by two paths and a member an earlier chunk's walk removed. The throw site of `CascadeBatchNarrowed` is before the first hook dispatch and outside the write `try`, and no middleware I read wraps what `next()` raises, so the walk's `instanceof` holds.

**Consumers that relied on per-row cascade hooks, read against the new shape:**
- plugin-auth last-admin guard (`resolveTargetIds`): asks `options.multi` first and resolves the target set from `options.where`, so a chunk is judged whole; with two chunks the last one refuses. Same verdict as the by-id walk. The diff's `[F1]` describe pins both legs on a real SQLite engine.
- plugin-sharing `record-share-cascade` / `rule-hooks`, service-storage `file-reference-lifecycle`: once-per-write work at `dispatch.index === 0` off the shared `dispatch.scope`; correct for a chunk.
- plugin-audit `writeAudit`, record-change triggers, `membership-ended-session`: per row off `previous`; unchanged.
- plugin-sharing `primary-bu-projection` (afterDelete, reads remaining memberships): intermediate writes differ, final state equal.
- Roll-ups: the batch hands `recomputeSummaries` the matched rows' foreign keys, once per chunk; the non-rollback outcome the changeset declares is the re-triaged fixture.

**Findings**

- **M1 · must-fix · the batch drops the read scope the by-id child delete enforces, so a child today's cascade refuses can be deleted.** Read, not run.
  - By-id leg, today: plugin-security step 2.7 runs for a nested by-id delete too (`extractSingleId`), and whenever a write-class filter binds it re-reads the row with `this.ql.findOne(object, { where: { $and: [{ id }, platformWritePredicate] }, context })`. That read goes through the read door, so select-class RLS, the sharing read filter and every data middleware's read visibility compose onto it; a hidden row comes back null and the delete answers 403, which rolls the whole cascade back.
  - Batch leg, this head: the predicate door composes the delete-class RLS (`computeLayeredRlsFilter(..., 'delete')`) and sharing's `buildWriteFilter(..., 'delete')` onto the AST. The readable-rows scope (`readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`, #21829) is added only when `addressedPredicateWrite` answers true, and it answers false for a nested write (`engineOperationScope`), which a cascade batch always is. `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` derives the write scope from the select narrowing only when NO write-class `using` policy applies; when one does (an authored delete policy, the in-domain ownership floor), the write scope is that policy alone.
  - So on an object where sharing abstains (a `public` model, no `owner_id`), with a delete-class `using` policy the child satisfies and a select-class policy that hides it, the engine's raw `driver.find(object, ast)` returns the child, the missing-id check in `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` passes, no `CascadeBatchNarrowed` is thrown, and the child is deleted. Today the same parent delete is refused 403 and nothing is deleted.
  - This contradicts ruling 6893104201 point (2), which 6893661036 kept ("a refused child rolls back the whole cascade"), epic #33631's rule ("read scope and tenant wall stay in the pushed-down statement"), the platform's own write-door rule (#7665, #21771: a row the caller cannot read is not written), the changeset's "Unchanged: ... a permission refusal rolls the whole cascade back", and the `deleteCascadedChildren` docblock, which states the fallback as covering the caller's scope. The missing-id check proves "never fewer" only.
  - Clears with either: a fix so a claimed batch also proves the chunk is what the by-id leg admits (for example the walk asks the caller's read door for the chunk's ids and falls back to by-id when any is missing; the by-id path then reproduces today's answer in both cases), with a both-legs pin on a real plugin-security stack; or that same pin, green on this head, showing the by-id leg also deletes, which would refute this reading. Either earns a delta review. #33782 merging without a pin for this shape does not clear it.

- **S1 · should-fix · a cascade whose child object is `sys_organization` is newly refused.** `delete()` throws `organizationPredicateDeleteRefusal` (409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`) for any organization delete not by id, before any hook. `deleteCascadedChildren` catches `CascadeBatchNarrowed` only, so that chunk no longer reaches the by-id path, where the per-organization delete (`refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned`, plugin-auth's clean-up) used to run. No shipped relation cascades into `sys_organization` (`parent_organization_id` is a plain lookup), so this needs an authored `cascade` relation on it; but it is a new refusal of a delete that works today, against ruling point (3), and the fix is one term in `batchable`. The general shape: any refusal the predicate arm raises that the by-id arm does not is now the cascade's answer.

- **N1 · nit · `hook.zod.ts`, `dispatch.mode` bullet, incomplete against the engine.** It names one fallback ("a chunk the caller's scope narrows is deleted by id instead and keeps 'record'"). The engine has two more: a driver with no `deleteMany`, and a floored external driver; on those every cascaded child stays `'record'`. And "every child's `beforeDelete` runs before any of them is gone" is true per chunk of 500 within one relation, not across chunks or relations; the changeset says "the chunk", the spec does not.
- **N2 · nit · `hook.zod.ts`, `referentialCascadeDelete`, "Why a declared key" is now stale.** "`ctx.user`, `ctx.session` and `ctx.input` are identical between a child the cascade removes and a user's hand delete of that same child" no longer holds on the batch path: `ctx.input.options` differs (`multi`, the chunk predicate), and so does `dispatch.mode`. The key's contract is untouched.
- **N3 · nit · changeset FROM → TO omits `ctx.result`.** In a cascaded child's `afterDelete` it was the driver's by-id answer and is now absent, as on every per-row delete context.
- **N4 · nit · the `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` comment "The read ran through the AST the middleware chain composed, so it is the caller's scope"** overstates: it is the caller's WRITE scope. This is the sentence M1 turns on; it should say which scope once M1 is settled.

N1 to N4 ride the re-push M1 forces; none of them alone would hold the round.

## Review — FAIL

Head-sha: `89dff98f61dd45bc47bef8b17d358db26676a759`
Area: S2 / A4 · Fixes #33699
Contract-review record: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/33887#issuecomment-6896079092 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: schema face `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` plus the narrowing face, from an isolated run). Its verdict is FAIL.

1. **M1 · must-fix · a nested cascade batch skips the read-door check.** `addressedPredicateWrite` returns `false` when `nested` is true. I spot-checked this in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts`, around lines 122–137. So a cascaded chunk deleted by predicate never passes through `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`.
   - What goes wrong: a child that select-class RLS hides, but that a delete-class `using` policy admits, is now deleted. On the old by-id leg the same child refused with 403 and the whole delete rolled back.
   - What it contradicts: rulings 6893104201 (2) and 6893661036, epic #33631, and the changeset's "Unchanged" line.
   - To clear it, do one of these:
     - check the chunk's ids against the read door, fall back to by-id for any chunk that check narrows, and add a both-legs pin on a real plugin-security stack; or
     - add a pin that refutes the scenario.
2. **S1 · should-fix · a cascade into `sys_organization` is newly refused.** `organizationPredicateDeleteRefusal` (409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`) fires before the by-id fallback, and `deleteCascadedChildren` catches only `CascadeBatchNarrowed`. This is a new refusal of a delete that works today. The fix is one term in `batchable`.
3. **N1–N4 · nits** (details in the record). They can ride the re-push that M1 forces:
   - N1: the fallback list under `dispatch.mode` is incomplete (it misses the no-`deleteMany` driver and the floored external driver), and "before any of them is gone" holds per chunk.
   - N2: the "Why a declared key" text on `referentialCascadeDelete` is stale.
   - N3: the changeset FROM → TO omits that `ctx.result` in a cascaded `afterDelete` is now absent.
   - N4: "the caller's scope" should say "the caller's write scope".
4. **Precondition · seat's call.** Ruling precondition (1) is not met. #33782, the security parity pins card, is still an open issue with no PR. This PR should not land ahead of it unless the seat waives that.
5. **Scope versus `Fixes`.** c1 (merging the three identical reads) is not done, but `Fixes #33699` closes the card. Either do c1 here, or change the keyword to `Part of #33699` and name where c1 goes.
6. **Clause-② / Metadata-protocol.** The claim says `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The record confirms that reading: `dispatch.mode` gains `'batch'` on cascaded children and `ctx.result` goes away. This is BREAKING-shaped, so the changeset's FROM → TO has to be complete (see N3) before it can pass.
7. **File surface.** In surface, apart from `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.test.ts`, which is a test-only edit outside the declared surface. It is acceptable, but name it in the claim's surface on the re-push.
8. **Check-runs at review time:** 54 success, 11 skipped, and Test Core (3/8) still in progress.

On the re-push, a delta review covers only M1, S1 and items 4 and 5. The record's re-review is scoped to the same items.

Test Core (8/8) is red at `7d2730a956c55bf529fcb29d1cc53ba819c79a2d`, and it was red at `eab93bab` too, on the same 4 cases in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cascade-delete-security-parity.test.ts` (blocks 2, 3, 3, 4). Each expects `landed` and gets 403 `FORBIDDEN`.

- Root cause, measured by the fix-round dev: plugin-sharing `inferTargetId` returns `where.id` even when it is `{ $in: [...] }`. The cascade batch `delete(child, { where: { id: { $in } }, multi: true })` on a private, owner-scoped object is therefore judged as a by-id write of `"[object Object]"`. It reproduces with this PR's read-door proof ablated, so the defect is in plugin-sharing, not in this diff.
- The fix is #33928's (S1). With this branch's earlier head plus that fix, the parity pins pass 8/8.
- This PR does not reshape its predicate to dodge it. Once #34033 merges, I'll merge `origin/main` here, re-read CI, and then request review-b's delta. The land order stays #33927 → #33928 → this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**The batch itself, against ruling 6893661036 (F1), read in the cited code.**

- Rows deleted. The walk collects a relation's `cascade` dependents over the whole root set (deduplicated, so a multi-valued child naming two roots goes once), filters each chunk against `entered` at issue time, and issues `delete(child, { where: { id: { $in } }, multi: true })`. The predicate arm deletes exactly the rows its scoped read returned, and the claimed batch refuses to proceed (`CascadeBatchNarrowed`, before any hook or write) unless that read returned every id asked for. So a batch removes the chunk or nothing; a short chunk goes by id and answers as today.
- Nested cascades, restrict and set_null siblings. A member chunk joins the root's set through `cascadeDeleteSets`, so the child's own relations are walked once for the chunk with the same restrict, set_null and required-escalation judgments as the by-id child delete, and grandchildren are batched in turn. Relation order is unchanged, and the pre-write `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade` is untouched. A row reached by two paths or by a self-reference is entered before the chunk's own walk and removed once.
- Multi-valued relations: the probe attribution and the member-removal write are untouched; only the `cascade` limb moved.
- Chunk boundaries: 500 per statement, under the per-row hook ceiling, pinned at 501.
- Transaction and partial failure: the batch runs inside the root's unit as the by-id child did; a before-phase or after-phase refusal rolls the cascade back (pinned on a driver that really rolls back). On a runtime that cannot roll back the whole chunk is gone where one child was; the changeset says so and the re-triaged fixture pins it.
- Recycle bin: the root's capture snapshots the collected set before the walk and a member opens no entry on either shape. One population differs: S2.
- Hooks: each child's `beforeDelete` and `afterDelete` run once with `previous` its own row and the marker in both phases (pinned, grandchildren included). The token claim is exact-set, single-use and taken before any middleware, so a hook's own delete is not marked.
- Roll-ups: the batch hands `recomputeSummaries` the matched rows once per chunk; same parents recomputed.
- Realtime: one `data.record.deleted` per child from its pre-image, never the bulk event (pinned).
- Audit and share clean-up per child: per row off `previous`; the test that proves it on the full stack (#33927 block 4) is one of the four red cases, so on this head it is read, not demonstrated.
- Security rules of the child. The rule: a cascade batch deletes no child the by-id delete of that child would refuse (delete permission, row scope, tenant wall), and refuses the whole cascade where the by-id delete refuses. Read scope and row-level write scope: kept, by the read-door proof plus the narrowed-batch check, on the plugin-security axis. Tenant wall: the same Layer 0 predicate rides the batch's AST and driver options. Record sharing: I found no path on which this tree deletes a child the by-id sharing gate refuses, and the parity block that would show it ("never more rows") is red at this head, so that direction is not demonstrated here.
